what: a countersunk O6.4 hole (O13.7, 90 deg) through a plate 0.15 mm from a wall standing on it: the countersink tool reached ~0.7 mm above the entry face and notched the wall
method: the countersink's rim (y = 23 + 6.85 = 29.85) stays clear of the wall (y = 30), so nothing above z = 8 changes. Plate 40x40x8 + wall 40x10x30 = 24800; the hole removes the O6.4 cylinder through 8 plus the countersink cone over it (depth (13.7-6.4)/2 = 3.65: pi h/3 (R^2+Rr+r^2) - pi r^2 h). Faces: bottom, the two L-shaped x faces, y=0, y=40 (plate and wall coplanar), the plate top, the wall's -y face and top, the cone and the bore = 10. Area: 7480 - pi 6.85^2 - pi 3.2^2 + pi (6.85+3.2) 3.65 sqrt2 + 2 pi 3.2 (8-3.65). The report's clearance M6 is given as its O6.4 so the answer doesn't depend on the clearance table
